v.why: Replacing a missing input edge with a 3x3 conv gives large gains (e.g. experiments 152, 166, 219, 262, 337, 392), more than replacing an existing conv.
Swapping a 3x3 conv for a 1x1 conv gives roughly zero or negative change (experiments 110, 92), while upgrading from pool, skip or none gives gains.
Going from 1x1 to 3x3 on edge 3 changes little or hurts (experiments 27, 124, 218, 395), while replacing none, skip or pool gives large gains.
Replacing a 3x3 conv on edge 3 with pooling causes big drops (experiments 202, 238, 321, 387).
Converting a pooling edge 1 to a 3x3 conv gives consistent gains (experiments 101, 115, 265, 329), larger than when edge 1 is already skip or conv.
Removing a skip edge 0 is near-neutral or positive (experiments 81, 299, 383), while removing a conv edge 0 is strongly harmful.
Replacing a 1x1 conv on edge 4 with skip tends to hurt (experiments 40, 51, 70, 264), while replacing pool or none is neutral or positive.
Removing a skip connection on edge 2 causes large drops (experiments 240, 261, 288), while removing a conv on edge 2 is about neutral.
Upgrading a skip edge 0 to a 1x1 conv gives solid gains (experiments 60, 97, 121), more than other starting ops.
Replacing a 3x3 conv on edge 0 with pooling is severely harmful (experiments 12, 308, 353, 370), unlike replacing other ops.

raw:
Most of these hypotheses come from reading the 400 experiments, not from a systematic fit. The strongest are those where several experiments agree across all three datasets. Examples are experiments 12, 353, 370 and 308 for edge 0 → avg_pool_3x3, and experiments 202, 238, 321 and 387 for edge 3 → avg_pool_3x3. Several are weaker. Edge 4 → skip_connect under e4=nor_conv_1x1 and edge 2 → none under e2=skip_connect each have counterexamples among the experiments.
